solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Potato chips ultimately followed by desert

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word chips

parts.note: read as dessert (the clue drops an s): a pudding, informally pud

explanation.surface: Someone eats potato chips and then moves on to a sweet course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' stands for 'dessert' here, whose British short form is PUD (pudding); 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'chips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is a common informal British word for a potato.

clue.text: Important part of diet for adolescent, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the letters come from how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: for gives PRO (in favour of) and an adolescent is a TEEN

explanation.surface: A nutrition tip about what a teenager should eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This nutrient, found in meat, eggs and beans, is a key component of any diet.

clue.text: Group of model Hindus found here

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken from inside the words model Hindus

explanation.surface: A city where you might find a community of exemplary Hindus.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'moDEL HIndus'; 'here' is the definition, the place named by the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital region is a place where many Hindus live, so it fits 'here' in this clue's scene.

clue.text: Slash cost of delicate material?

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: A question about cutting the price of fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash something is to cut or tear it deeply, a synonym of the verb answer.

clue.text: Allow any number to ignore period of fasting

indicators.note: to ignore means a letter of the fasting period is left out

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
N is the maths symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Permission to skip a religious fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to permit, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Policeman's list of wrong-doers

parts.note: cons are convicts, criminals
a table is a list or chart

explanation.surface: A police officer's register of criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer of the lowest rank in Britain holds this title.

clue.text: Dog hunting vermin traps large snake

indicators.note: traps means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a ratter is a dog used to catch rats
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A terrier out after rats catches a big snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattlesnakes are informally called this, after the sound their tails make.

clue.text: Cosmetic contained in compact, one realises

indicators.note: contained in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone realises a make-up compact holds a beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'compacT ONE Realises'.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin product, applied after cleansing, is a type of cosmetic.

clue.text: Form of classical language got Linda confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of got Linda are jumbled

explanation.surface: Linda muddled her Latin lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jocular mock-Latin, a debased imitation of the classical tongue.

clue.text: A teachers' union recalled one in school

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: A union official is called back to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a place of learning, but it is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in schools, and this large fish is one member of such a group.

clue.text: Legendary creature still seen to west of island

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A mythical beast still spotted on the western edge of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature of legend.

clue.text: Colonists, people who pay their debts

definitions.meaning: colonists are people who make a new home in a new land
those who clear a bill or account

explanation.surface: Pioneers who also pay what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneers colonising land and those squaring accounts both share the one word, from two senses of the verb.

clue.text: Class having old-fashioned aid for technical drawing

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as in a school ability set
square means conventional, out of date

explanation.surface: A school class still using dated drawing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular instrument is used by draughtsmen to draw angles.

clue.text: Type of play broadcast all at once

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of at once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drama transmitted in its entirety in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: A short drama with only a single act is a recognised type of play.

clue.text: One enthralled by a celebrated English dancer

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the following pieces

parts.note: a star is someone celebrated
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a famous English dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire was American, so 'English' is misleading as a description of the dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred, the Hollywood star of Top Hat, was a famous dancer.

clue.text: American composer responsible for Hair?

definitions.meaning: Samuel, US composer of the Adagio for Strings
a hairdresser for men, who cuts hair; Hair is also a famous musical

explanation.surface: Asking which American composer wrote the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair' suggests the rock musical, but the second definition is a man who cuts hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel of that surname was an American composer, and a men's hairdresser looks after hair.

clue.text: Resilient characters from Castile

indicators.note: characters from means the letters of Castile are used to form a new word

explanation.surface: Tough people from the Spanish region of Castile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy springs back into shape, so it is resilient.

clue.text: Secret fascination of Miss Wood, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the letters come from a phrase spoken aloud

parts.note: miss gives MISS and a wood is TEAK

explanation.surface: The alluring air of a woman called Miss Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means an aura of mystery and glamour, a secret allure.

clue.text: Long period of time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time passing before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective attached to 'period', but it is the verb meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Portion of corn served with soft fruit

indicators.note: served with means one piece is placed alongside the other

parts.note: P is the music abbreviation for piano, soft
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a corn plant

explanation.surface: A helping of corn on the plate with soft fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common orchard fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Dad taking teacher around European capital

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A father showing a teacher around a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Vehicle returned at eleven

indicators.note: returned means the word at is written backwards

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A car came back at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a vehicle for hire.

clue.text: A box containing copper? Absolutely right

indicators.note: containing means the box holds the metal inside it

parts.note: a crate is a box
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a box with a policeman inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact and correct is absolutely right.

clue.text: Initially censor's unlikely to make incisions

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A censor is at first reluctant to make cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice into something is to make incisions.

clue.text: Money to be made in half-term holiday

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of the word term

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Earning cash during the school half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-term' reads as a school break, but 'half' takes TE from 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: A savings account pays interest, the money earned on deposits.

clue.text: Unwell and so weak in the end

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, used to mark a quotation as written

indicators.note: in the end picks out the last letter of the word weak

explanation.surface: Someone ill and therefore eventually weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill and poorly both describe being unwell, a plain synonym.
